title: The gates bite with --ack as the recorded override for D3, D5, D6
context: DEFINE step 3 train (spec 2026-10-01) brings the substantive checks of proposal 3.2 into D3, D5 and D6 across PRs 5, 6 and 7. The 0.29.0 posture left those stages warn-with-ack: --check exits 0 with a stderr [warn] line, --ack as the recorded override. The spec section 4 gates-bite intro and decision 9 both pin the biting posture: --check exits 4 on D3, D5 and D6 as it does on blocking stages; --ack stays as the recorded override for those three because the ruleset's recordedInChain channel needs it (decision 8's pattern applied to gates, not retired with the verb). The compute remains pure; readiness.js collects candidate paths and the CLI resolves them on disk so the gate functions see a resolvedPaths map in the stage context. PR 5 lands the three D3 bite checks (shapes:templateMarkers, shapes:entityJoin, shapes:pathsResolve), the ackable(stage) companion to stagePolicy, and the --check shapes exit 4 policy; PRs 6 and 7 bite D5 and D6 on the same shape.
decision: The gates bite with --ack as the recorded override for D3, D5 and D6. stagePolicy returns warnWithAck for D3, D5 and D6 and blocking for D1, D2, D4, D7 and D8 (ruling R4 2026-10-05: the honest label for an ackable stage is warnWithAck, and the viewer pill vocabulary and the CLI text report both key off that; the pre-R4 wording that said stagePolicy returned blocking for every stage with a separate ackable() is retired because it was never true in code, and ackable(stage) stays only as the sibling helper that the CLI --check and freeze verbs read to decide whether a failing stage honours an acknowledgement at the current hash). The readiness CLI --check <stage> policy follows that split: on a blocking stage, a failing state exits 4 (today's behaviour); on a warnWithAck stage, a failing state exits 4 unless the freeze record acknowledges that gate at the current tree hash, in which case it exits 0. --ack on any blocking stage stays a usage refusal with exit 2 (D1, D2, D4, D7, D8). The three D3 bite checks ship as pure engineer checks on src/query/gates.js: shapes:templateMarkers over delta (per-kind marker presence on interfaces[].description, ids <tacId>:<name>, why names the missing marker, drafts included), shapes:entityJoin over tree (every coreEntities[].name named by exactly one recordShape, ids TAD.entity:<name>; ruling R5 2026-10-05: the check evaluates before any scope early-return, via the shared helper ADR-4138 lands), shapes:pathsResolve over delta (any path:-like token resolves on disk against the resolvedPaths map in the stage context or the description carries authoredAt: D3; ruling R6 2026-10-05: the token scanner also honours a short whitelist of known bare repo names -- Dockerfile, Makefile, LICENSE, Procfile, Containerfile, Justfile, Rakefile, Gemfile, CODEOWNERS -- so the slash-or-extension rule stops silently skipping them). Validate findings only where a legacy tree can comply; the dogfood tree records any residual failure in KNOWN GAPS rather than weakening the check.
consequences: A failing D3 bite now blocks CI unless the engineer either fixes the tree or writes a recorded override with --ack --reason at the current hash; the record stays visible in the freeze record (the chain of recordedInChain the ruleset reads). stagePolicy returns warnWithAck for D3/D5/D6 and blocking for D1/D2/D4/D7/D8 (ruling R4): the viewer pill vocabulary reads that directly, and the CLI --check text output names the policy label alongside the stage state. The readyToBuild fold stays unchanged because the fold reads the stage state (passed | failing | acknowledged | notApplicable), not the stage policy. The gate functions stay pure: the CLI is the module that resolves candidate paths on disk and the stage context carries the resolved map. The D3 bite surfaces three new engineer checks on the readiness tab and the text report; nothing on the productOwner side moves. --level intent and --level build exits are unchanged because the levels fold is already a derived view. Ruling R5 (shapes:entityJoin unconditional) and ruling R7 (skeleton:standardsCited tree-wide regardless of D2 scope) land through ADR-4138's shared helper, so a narrowed D2 or D3 scope that excludes every item in the local scope still reports the tree-wide finding instead of returning notApplicable. The dogfood tree keeps CI green by scoping its own readiness call as it already does; the three new checks pass on the dogfood chain because the shipped TACs name their markers truthfully.

alternativesConsidered.name: Retire --ack (make D3, D5, D6 plain blocking)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Drop the --ack verb everywhere and let a failing D3, D5 or D6 simply block CI with no override.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The ruleset's recordedInChain channel exists so a refuse at a hash can be acknowledged with a reason that becomes part of the chain. The gates bite is decision 8's pattern applied to gates (refuse with a recorded override), and retiring --ack removes the channel the ruleset depends on. The spec decision 9 pins this; this ADR records it in-chain.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep warn-with-ack: --check exits 0 with a [warn] on D3, D5, D6
alternativesConsidered.summary: Leave the 0.29.0 posture in place; let the bite only surface in validate and the viewer.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The whole point of the DEFINE step 3 train is to make D3, D5 and D6 bite: the substantive checks of proposal 3.2 land here, and CI must refuse on them for the engineer to feel the gate. Warn-with-ack kept them a soft signal; the spec moves them to blocking with --ack as the recorded override.

alternativesConsidered.name: Make the gate functions impure and resolve paths inline
alternativesConsidered.summary: Let shapes:pathsResolve open the filesystem directly so the gate module decides path existence on its own.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: gates.js is the one pure module every surface composes; folding I/O into it would re-couple the viewer and the CLI through disk access. The CLI already owns the project-root resolve for the walker and the ledgers; adding one more resolve step for candidate paths is a one-pass walk, and the stage context grows by one map. The viewer uses the same seam when it renders the Readiness tab server-side.
